contenido: Recent results show that Colombia scored 383, 409, and 411 points, ranking 64 out of 81 participating countries. These figures highlight the need for structural reforms in the education system.
The average for OECD countries stood at 472, 476, and 485 points. This mean serves as a global benchmark for evaluating the development of fundamental skills in students.
Singapore leads global measurements with outstanding scores of 575, 543, and 561. Its pedagogical approach remains a model of excellence and innovation.
The region faces significant challenges in closing learning gaps. Investment in teacher training is crucial to improving long-term indicators.
To move forward, it is essential to integrate technology into the classroom and foster critical thinking, adapting the curriculum to 21st-century demands.
